alex: Heads-up — I opened a docs PR with an example for the onprem installer that covers three small but confusing edge cases we keep getting questions about: systemd unit tweaks for offline bundles, MTU/sysctl notes for SR‑IOV NICs, and an example of using a unix socket to talk to the local HSM/KMS agent when customers are air‑gapped. PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/389 (draft).

maya: Nice. Can you paste the critical snippets here? I'll sanity-check the commands. :eyes:

alex: Sure — copied from the PR. first, systemd unit fragment we suggest adding so the installer waits for the offline bundle mount (avoids race during upgrades):

```
[Unit]
Description=Redwood Installer (wait for bundle)
After=network-online.target local-fs.target
Wants=ntp.service

[Service]
Type=oneshot
ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/redwood-install --apply-offline /mnt/offline-bundle
RemainAfterExit=true

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
```

alex: Then a short sysctl/MTU note we added — SR‑IOV VF devices sometimes default to 1500 while host expects 9000; recommend explicit set in docs and a one‑liner to persist:```
sudo sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_forward=1
sudo ip link set dev eth0 mtu 9000
# persist via /etc/sysctl.d/99-redwood.conf and /etc/network/interfaces or distro equivalent
```

jorge: Quick question — should we call out iptables/nft ordering for kube-proxy on those MTU lanes? I remember a case where conntrack timed out because the pod cidr was mismatched.

alex: good call, added a short note: "verify podCIDR matches CNI and conntrack max" and a troubleshooting command: `conntrack -S` and `ss -tnp | grep kube-proxy`

li-wei: About the unix socket example for KMS/HSM — love it. Can you show the SDK snippet? we should make sure it's consistent with our python/js SDKs.

alex: here's a minimal JSON example we added to the quickstart (embedded in docs as a code block):

```
# example: local kms proxy via unix socket
{
  "kms": {
    "type": "unix_socket",
    "socket_path": "/var/run/redwood-kms/proxy.sock",
    "ca_bundle": "/etc/redwood/ca.pem",
    "auth_token_env": "REDWOOD_KMS_TOKEN"
  },
  "hsm": {
    "pkcs11_module": "/usr/lib/libpkcs11.so",
    "slot": "0",
    "pin_env": "HSM_PIN"
  }
}
```

li-wei: For the python SDK we prefer env-first patterns. Might add a note that if socket_path is not present fallback to TCP host:port, but for airgapped installs we always prefer socket.

maya: doc/style question — do we need an explicit step to `chmod` the socket so the installer (running as redwood user) can access it? I think yes.

alex: yep — added a short step: `chown redwood:redwood /var/run/redwood-kms/proxy.sock && chmod 660 /var/run/redwood-kms/proxy.sock`

docs-bot: CI check — code block style OK, missing link check for /etc/redwood/ca.pem reference (warn).

alex: thanks bot — fixed link to the cert path anchor in the same doc (now uses relative anchor `#certificate-bundles`).

jorge: small nit — in the systemd unit you used `ntp.service`. For distros using systemd-timesyncd maybe better to `Wants=systemd-timesyncd.service` or just remove Wants.

alex: good point — I'll change to `Wants=systemd-timesyncd.service` and add a note about NTP being optional.

li-wei: overall looks solid. Can you also add a short troubleshooting checklist at the bottom for air‑gapped KMS issues? e.g., verify socket exists, permissions, cert chain, correct pin/slot mapping, and HSM vendor logs.

alex: added a 6‑item checklist and a one‑line debug command for the HSM PKCS#11 test: `pkcs11-tool --module /usr/lib/libpkcs11.so -L`

maya: LGTM from docs side. I'll give final review once you update the systemd Wants and the chmod note. :+1:

alex: updated and pushed to PR 389. marking for final pass — @maya @li-wei please approve when you can. thanks everyone! :rocket:
